newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ADAMS LATEST IN ARSENAL TALE OF WOE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ADAMS LATEST IN ARSENAL TALE OF WOE.

text.p: Tony Adams is the latest in a string of Arsenal stars to hit the headlines off the field.
George Graham, the most successful manager in the club's 110-year history, recently completed a year's ban from the game for accepting cash "bungs" over transfers. He is now at Leeds.

Adams's close personal friend Paul Merson, a fellow England international, admitted snorting cocaine as well as an addiction to gambling and drink. Merson underwent treatment in a clinic and a lengthy ban.
Midfielder David Hillier lowered the club's image this year when he was fined for stealing luggage at Gatwick Airport.
Another midfielder Ray Parlour was also fined by a court after a punch-up with a Hong Kong cabbie on a club tour.
Like Adams, other Arsenal stars have landed in the dock for drink-driving. Striker Kevin Campbell, Scots international Charlie Nicholas and Merson were all prosecuted.
Five players were fined and sent home from a club holiday after a drinking session before a 1990 game against Norwich.
